findings.evidence: Mathlib/Algebra/Lie/Sl2.lean:160 `lemma lie_h_pow_toEnd_f (n : ℕ)` (all `n`) vs :170 `lemma lie_e_pow_succ_toEnd_f (n : ℕ) : ⁅e, ψ (n + 1)⁆ = …` — the same distinction, in the same subject area, and the module doc of this PR cites both.
findings.fix: Add `_succ` to the eight successor-only names: `e_mul_f_pow_succ`, `f_mul_e_pow_succ`, `e_mul_f_dividedPower_succ`, `f_mul_e_dividedPower_succ`, `ι_e_mul_ι_f_pow_succ`, `ι_f_mul_ι_e_pow_succ`, `ι_e_mul_dividedPower_succ_ι_f`, `ι_f_mul_dividedPower_succ_ι_e`.
findings.issue: `e_mul_f_pow`, `f_mul_e_pow` (l.148), `e_mul_f_dividedPower` (l.192), `f_mul_e_dividedPower` (l.198), `ι_e_mul_ι_f_pow` (l.231), `ι_f_mul_ι_e_pow` (l.237), `ι_e_mul_dividedPower_ι_f` (l.262) and `ι_f_mul_dividedPower_ι_e` (l.269) are all stated only at index `n + 1`, but carry the same name shape as the siblings `h_mul_f_pow`/`h_mul_e_pow`/`h_mul_f_dividedPower`/`h_mul_e_dividedPower`/`ι_h_mul_ι_f_pow`/`ι_h_mul_dividedPower_ι_f`, which genuinely hold for every `n`. The name advertises a stronger indexing than the statement has.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Basic.lean:219 `lemma mul_pow (a b : M) : ∀ n, (a * b) ^ n = a ^ n * b ^ n`; Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Commute/Defs.lean:167 `lemma mul_pow (h : Commute a b)`; TauCeti/RingTheory/DividedPowers/Associative.lean:155 `theorem mul_dividedPower (m n : ℕ) (x : A)`.
findings.fix: Spell the conclusion out so the prefix cannot be misread, e.g. `mul_pow_eq_pow_mul_add_zsmul` and `mul_dividedPower_eq_dividedPower_mul_add_zsmul` (keeping an `_of_commutator_eq_zsmul` clause only if still needed for disambiguation).
findings.issue: `mul_pow_of_commutator_eq_zsmul` reads as a hypothesised form of the root lemma `mul_pow : (a * b) ^ n = a ^ n * b ^ n` — exactly the shape `Commute.mul_pow` already occupies — but proves `x * y ^ n = y ^ n * x + (n * c) • y ^ n`. Same problem at l.225: `mul_dividedPower_of_commutator_eq_zsmul` reuses the prefix `mul_dividedPower`, which at l.155 of this same file already means `dividedPower m x * dividedPower n x = choose (m+n) m • dividedPower (m+n) x`.

findings.evidence: All eight statements have the form `_ * dividedPower n _ = …`; compare l.164 `H * dividedPower n F = …` with l.276 `ι ℚ h * dividedPower n (ι ℚ f) = …`.
findings.fix: Use the term order throughout: `h_mul_dividedPower_f`, `h_mul_dividedPower_e`, `e_mul_dividedPower_f`, `f_mul_dividedPower_e`, matching the `ι_` group.
findings.issue: Two word orders for the identical term shape `X * dividedPower n Y` in one file: `h_mul_f_dividedPower` (l.163), `h_mul_e_dividedPower` (l.172), `e_mul_f_dividedPower` (l.192), `f_mul_e_dividedPower` (l.198) suffix the operation, while `ι_h_mul_dividedPower_ι_f` (l.275), `ι_h_mul_dividedPower_ι_e` (l.280), `ι_e_mul_dividedPower_ι_f` (l.262), `ι_f_mul_dividedPower_ι_e` (l.269) infix it. The names are not guessable from either half of the file.

summary: The successor-indexed relations are named as if they held for every exponent, contrary to the `pow_succ` convention Mathlib's own sl₂ file uses (`lie_e_pow_succ_toEnd_f` vs `lie_h_pow_toEnd_f`); and two new general lemmas reuse the prefixes `mul_pow` and `mul_dividedPower`, which already denote different statements in Mathlib root and in the same TauCeti namespace.
